config.title: Regular Expressions

intro.title: Regular Expressions
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple email validator that checks if user input matches a valid email format. You'll learn how to create and use regular expressions (regex) to search for patterns in text. The main technologies involved are JavaScript's RegExp object and string methods like test() and match(). You'll practice writing regex patterns with special characters to define rules for valid email addresses. By the end, you'll understand how regex can help validate different types of text input in real applications.
intro.usecase: Regular expressions are essential for validating and processing user input in real-world web applications. For example, they are used in sign-up forms to ensure email addresses and phone numbers follow correct formats, in search bars to implement advanced filtering on dashboards, and in content editors to find and replace text patterns. As a developer, you'll use regex to sanitize data, parse log files, and enforce input rules across interactive UI components like modals, settings panels, and data tables.

objectives: Construct a regular expression literal using forward slashes
Apply the test() method to check if a pattern matches a string
Implement the match() method to extract substrings that match a pattern
Configure character classes to match specific sets of characters
Manipulate strings using the replace() method with regular expressions
Initialize a RegExp object with dynamic patterns using the constructor
Control pattern matching behavior using flags like 'g' and 'i'

steps.title: Add input elements and wire event handlers for text and pattern
steps.instruction: Inside your App component's return statement, add two input elements: one for text input with value={text} and onChange={handleTextChange}, and another for pattern input with value={pattern} and onChange={handlePatternChange}.
steps.hint: Use <input> elements with type='text'. Connect the first input's value to the text state and its onChange to handleTextChange. Connect the second input's value to the pattern state and its onChange to handlePatternChange.

// Adding controlled input elements
<input type='text' value={someState} onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: Two text input fields appear in the UI: one for entering text to match against, and another for entering the regular expression pattern. Both inputs are controlled components that update their respective state values when typed into.
successCriteria: Two <input> elements are present in the return statement. The first input has value={text} and onChange={handleTextChange}. The second input has value={pattern} and onChange={handlePatternChange}.
